spreads.game: North Carolina Tar Heels @ UConn Huskies
facts: North Carolina +3.9 (53rd) vs UConn -0.2 (72nd), home edge +2.3
23rd by grade, 6th in Explosiveness, 45th in Success Rate
paras: Book has North Carolina laying eight on the road. The rating has them winning by 1.8 and the points check, built only from each team's own 2026 scoring and home field, has UConn winning by 5.5. The two disagree about who wins and agree completely about the number.

UConn score more than the team laying eight points on them. They put up 34.4 a game against North Carolina's 25.8, their offence grades 82.3 and ranks 23rd nationally and 6th in Explosiveness, and they are 5-2-1 against the spread, 17th in the country. Both teams are 4-4.

North Carolina's case rests on defence: 87.1 coverage, 27th, and 5th in Explosiveness allowed. That is a real edge against a UConn passing game that lives on big plays. But their own offence ranks 125th in Explosiveness and scores under 26 a game. Eight points asks a team that struggles to pull away to pull away on the road.

Rutgers are 2-6 and the record is the reason the number is this big, but they score 27.8 a game and rank 9th nationally in offensive Explosiveness. They have gone over in six of eight. A team that reaches the high twenties with big plays available is not the profile that gets held to a field goal.

spreads.game: Oklahoma State Cowboys @ Kansas State Wildcats
facts: Oklahoma State +12.1 (27th) vs Kansas State +7.5 (45th), home edge +2.8
2.8 points, the largest of the five
20th in Success Rate, 17th in Havoc, 135th in Explosiveness allowed
41.1 points a game, 6th in Success Rate, 100th in Explosiveness
paras: Book has Kansas State +6.5 at home. The rating has Oklahoma State by 1.8 and the points check has Kansas State winning by 0.7. Both land inside the number, and the home field here is worth 2.8 points, the largest in this group.

Kansas State defend the thing Oklahoma State do. The Cowboys rank 6th in offensive Success Rate nationally and score 41.1 a game. They rank 100th in Explosiveness, so they move methodically. Kansas State rank 20th in defensive Success Rate and 17th in Havoc, which is the unit built to interrupt exactly that, and they allow 21.9 points a game against Oklahoma State's 27.1.

The market is pricing the records. Oklahoma State are 5-3 and 6-2 against the spread, 7th in the country; Kansas State are 4-4 and 3-4-1 against it. That is the shape of team the number follows rather than leads, and both measures say six and a half is at least four points too many.

spreads.game: Colorado Buffaloes @ Arizona State Sun Devils
facts: Arizona State +1.4 (64th) vs Colorado -4.2 (90th), home edge +3.0
21.0 points a game, 108th in Success Rate, 132nd in Finishing Drives
paras: The one position here that lays a price. Book has Arizona State -3.5, the rating has it at 8.6 and the points check at 7.2, so both sit several points past the number on the same side.

Colorado cannot score. They put up 21.0 points a game on an offence ranked 108th in Success Rate and 132nd in Finishing Drives, and they rank 134th in offensive Field Position and tied 126th on defence, so they begin badly at both ends. Their 55.6 tackling grade ranks 123rd.

Arizona State are not a strong team at 4-4 and 29.5 points a game. What they are is better than this opponent in the places that decide a three-and-a-half-point game: 88.2 on defence against Colorado's 82.6, 79.3 tackling against 55.6, and three points of home field. The standing exclusion does not apply, because Colorado are 2-5-1 against the spread, 127th. This is not laying into a team the market has been underrating.

SP+ separates these two by 1.4 points and the market asks for five and a half. Home field at Purdue is worth only 1.8, which leaves the rating at Purdue by 3.2 and the points check at 2.9. Both sit inside the number.

Purdue are the nominal favourite and the weaker team on the sheet. They grade 72.1 overall, 118th in the country, with a defence at 68.9 that ranks 125th and a coverage grade of 46.3 that ranks 135th. They are 3-5 and allow 32.1 points a game.

Maryland bring the one unit that exploits that. Their pass rush grades 83.1, 15th nationally, against a Purdue offence ranked 62nd in Success Rate, and their special teams grade 90.2, 4th in the country, which is where a one-score game between two 100th-ranked teams usually turns. Both sides are 3-5 against the spread, so neither is being carried by its record.

props.game: Miami Hurricanes @ Notre Dame Fighting Irish
facts: 33 targets, 4.1 a game, 24 receptions over 184 routes
12.1 average depth of target, 2.34 yards per route run, 72.7 route grade, long of 61
paras: Gilbert averages 53.8 receiving yards a game against a 31.5 line, 22.3 yards of margin on his own rate. The projection discounts heavily for the opponent and still lands at 44.1.

Four targets a game is modest, but almost all of them count: 24 receptions on 33 targets is a 73 percent catch rate at a 12.1-yard average depth of target, producing 17.9 yards a catch with 2.34 yards per route run and a long of 61. Two catches clear the number.

Miami arrive 8-0 with the top-ranked offence in the country by grade, but their defence ranks 71st and their coverage grade of 62.5 ranks 119th, by some distance the softest part of an otherwise excellent team. Notre Dame are laying seven in a game posted at 54.5, and Miami are taken to cover that number elsewhere in this card; a close, high-scoring game is the script both positions want.
